facts: $1\text{ mL}$ of water takes up exactly $1\text{ cm}^3$ of space.
A bigger rise means a bigger object; the same rise means equal volumes.
steps: Read the water level **before** the object goes in.
Read the water level **after** the object is fully submerged.
Subtract: the rise is the object's volume.

foundation.solution_text:
$315\text{ mL}-240\text{ mL}=75\text{ mL}$
The stone has a volume of $75\text{ cm}^3$.

$542\text{ mL}-500\text{ mL}=42\text{ mL}$
The keyring has a volume of $42\text{ cm}^3$.

foundation.question_text:
Object A raises the water level by $60$ mL and object B raises it by $85$ mL.
Which has the greater volume?
foundation.solution_text: Object B has the greater volume because it causes the larger rise.

foundation.question_text:
Two objects each raise the water level by $35$ mL.
Compare their volumes.
foundation.solution_text: They have equal volumes: each displaces $35$ mL of water.

$260\text{ mL}-180\text{ mL}=80\text{ mL}$
The shell has a volume of $80\text{ cm}^3$.

foundation.question_text: Why must an object be fully submerged when its volume is measured by displacement?
foundation.solution_text: Only the submerged part displaces water, so full submersion is needed to measure the whole volume.

development.solution_text:
$804\text{ mL}-675\text{ mL}=129\text{ mL}$
The metal piece has a volume of $129\text{ cm}^3$.

development.question_text:
A bead raises water from $320$ mL to $347$ mL.
A bolt raises fresh water from $410$ mL to $452$ mL.
Which object is larger and by how much?
development.solution_text:
Bead: $347-320=27\text{ cm}^3$
Bolt: $452-410=42\text{ cm}^3$
$42-27=15\text{ cm}^3$
The bolt is larger by $15\text{ cm}^3$.

development.question_text:
Three objects displace $48$ mL, $51$ mL and $48$ mL.
Order their volumes and identify any equal pair.
development.solution_text:
$51\text{ cm}^3>48\text{ cm}^3=48\text{ cm}^3$
The first and third objects have equal volumes.

$430\text{ mL}+96\text{ mL}=526\text{ mL}$
The after-reading is $526$ mL.

development.question_text:
A cork floats with half of it above the water.
Would the rise show the cork’s full volume?
Explain.
development.solution_text: No. The rise shows only the volume of the submerged part, so the whole cork must be held fully under water.

development.question_text:
A student subtracts the after-reading from the before-reading and gets a negative result.
Diagnose the error.
development.solution_text: The order is reversed. Object volume is the new level minus the starting level, which gives a positive rise.

mastery.question_text:
Object P changes a level from $0.850$ L to $0.932$ L. Object Q displaces $79$ mL.
Which has the larger volume?
mastery.solution_text: P displaces $0.932-0.850=0.082\text{ L}=82\text{ mL}$. P is larger than Q by $3$ mL.

mastery.question_text:
A container reads $760$ mL after two objects of volumes $45\text{ cm}^3$ and $68\text{ cm}^3$ are submerged together.
Find the starting level.
mastery.solution_text:
$45+68=113\text{ mL}$
$760-113=647\text{ mL}$
The starting level was $647$ mL.

mastery.question_text:
A stone is measured twice: $300$ mL to $372$ mL, then $500$ mL to $571$ mL.
Explain why the results need checking.
mastery.solution_text: The rises are $72$ mL and $71$ mL. The same stone should displace the same volume, so one reading or graduation was inaccurate.
